headline_finding.statement: Across the 14 Paraguayan departments with sufficient MAG yield data (2007/08-2024/25), the 2 Occidental Chaco departments (Alto Paraguay, Boqueron) show a mean soy-yield trajectory of 109.96 kg/ha/yr vs 56.47 kg/ha/yr for the 12 Oriental departments — a ratio of 1.95x (descriptive only; n=2 Occidental is too small for inferential claims). The Occidental region also has higher indigenous community density (43.0 vs 30.6 communities/dept) but only 24% of the national total of 557 communities.

interpretation: The per-region comparison is DESCRIPTIVE (n=2 Occidental departments), not inferential. The cross-department Pearson correlation between historical mean yield and yield-trajectory slope is r=-0.306 (r^2=0.093, n=14), which is NOT statistically significant. This means: across the 14 departments with data, we do NOT see evidence that higher indigenous-community density → faster yield trajectory. The frontier expansion pattern is more parsimoniously explained by yield convergence: departments with lower historical yield (Misiones, Concepcion, Canindeyu) are catching up, while high-yield frontier departments (Alto Parana, Caaguazu, Itapua) continue expanding. This is consistent with the 'land rush' framing in Wesz Junior (2026) but does NOT support a causal claim linking indigenous community density to soy expansion.
limitations: Occidental slope rests on n=2 departments (Alto Paraguay, Boqueron). Presidente Hayes has no continuous yield data and is excluded. Per-region ratio is descriptive, not a hypothesis test.

Per-department indigenous community count is UNKNOWN — only Region Oriental/Occidental totals are in the INE 2022 Cuadro C1 substrate. The 'indi_density_per_dept' metric divides regional totals by regional department counts (a coarse proxy).
MAG yield data covers 2007/08-2024/25 (18 years); Cordillera has only 6 years and several other departments have gaps in earlier years. The slope computation requires >=5 years per department.
Cross-department regression n=14 is small for an inferential claim. The r=-0.306 / p=0.27 finding is reported but does not reject the null of no association at conventional thresholds.
No causal inference attempted. Departmental correlation is not causation; land-use drivers (commodity prices, road infrastructure, soil quality) are not controlled for.
